The three groups are accordion sections, each collapsible on its own. A section's heading is a row 28 pixels tall, on the theme's raised surface, a step apart from the rows: a chevron at its left, pointing right while collapsed and down while expanded, then its title and count, then, at its right, its own controls, Previous's filter and batch actions and Queued's auto-send switch and "Send next". Clicking the heading, anywhere but its controls, expands or collapses that section alone; any number can be expanded at once, and collapsing one takes its rows away and leaves only its heading. Previous starts collapsed and Running and Queued expanded, each time a project is opened; otherwise each stays as it was left while the application runs, each open project keeping its own. A collapsed section still counts its tasks, its controls still work, and opening one of its tasks from elsewhere, as from the running activity list, expands it to show that task.
All three headings are always in view, however far the tab is scrolled, so each section's controls are always in reach. A heading whose section starts above the visible rows is pinned at the top of the tab, and one whose section starts below them is pinned at its bottom, in their order: scrolled down into Running, the Previous heading is pinned at the top, the Running heading beneath it, and the Queued heading at the bottom; scrolled into Queued, Previous and Running are pinned at the top, one beneath the other. A heading never pushes another out of view; they stack, each 28 pixels, so the rows scroll in the space left between the headings pinned above and below. A heading in its place among the rows sits there as any row does, and is pinned only once its place leaves the visible rows. Clicking a pinned heading, anywhere but its chevron and controls, scrolls the list to that section's start; clicking its chevron expands or collapses it, as clicking a heading in its place does.
Each heading carries its section's controls, whichever place it is pinned in: Previous's selection, its "N selected", its batch actions, "Send N to Spec", "Send N to Code", and "Clear", while any task is selected, and its filter dropdown; Running's "Cancel all", while more than one task runs; and Queued's auto-send switch and "Send next". Where a heading is too narrow for all of them, its title gives way first, cut off with an ellipsis, and then its count, never its controls, the batch actions folding into a "N selected" menu once even that isn't enough.
A pinned heading draws over the rows with its own surface, never letting them show through, and is drawn once, never twice where it is pinned and where it lies. Previous's day divider sticks just below the Previous heading only while Previous's rows are what is in view beneath it.

#### Days
A day's divider is sticky beneath Previous's own heading: while its tasks are scrolled through, it stays pinned just below that heading, until the next day's divider pushes it out, so the day of the rows in view always shows. Day dividers take the place of the session dividers the previous tasks had; a session that starts a new conversation shows a small muted mark at its first row's right instead, its tooltip saying it started a new conversation.
 A heading whose section starts above the visible rows is pinned at the top of the tab, and one whose section starts below them is pinned at its bottom, in their order: scrolled down into Running, the Previous heading is pinned at the top, the Running heading beneath it, and the Queued heading at the bottom; scrolled into Queued, Previous and Running are pinned at the top, one beneath the other.
 A pinned heading sits over the list without moving any row, so where each row lies is unchanged by it.
 Headings pinned at the bottom take room from the list's visible area, as those at the top do, so scrolled to the bottom, the last row still shows whole above any heading pinned there, and none ever hides a row.

content.text:
All three section headings in the Tasks tab now stay in view with their controls, wherever you scroll. Before, each heading pushed the previous one out. The build is clean and a new test checks the stacking. Everything else passes except `long_output_is_measured_a_few_rows_a_frame`, which failed in the full run and passed on its own in earlier runs.

- **Stacking:** a heading whose section has scrolled up past the view pins to the top, and one whose section is still below pins to the bottom, in order. Scrolled into Previous, for example, Previous sits at the top with Running and Queued stacked at the bottom.
- **Controls on every heading:**
  - Previous: the selection count, Send N to Spec, Send N to Code, Clear, and the filter.
  - Running: a new "Cancel all", shown while more than one task runs.
  - Queued: auto-send and Send next.
- **Narrow headings:** the title shortens first, then the count. If the controls still don't fit, Previous's batch actions fold into an "N selected" menu.
- **Clicking:** clicking a pinned heading jumps to the start of its section. The chevron expands or collapses the section.
- **Day divider:** it still sticks just below Previous's heading, only while Previous's rows are in view.

At the sidebar's default width (260px) Previous's controls don't all fit, so its batch actions will usually show as the "N selected" menu until you widen the sidebar. Four existing selection tests expected them unfolded, so their test sidebar is now 420px wide.

The change is in `src/prompt_mode/tasks_tab.rs`.
